why.statement: Information may be abundant. Legibility is not.
why.asks: What can citizens now learn about the institutions that govern them, and how they shape places over time?
why.body:
Civic interplay exists to shape conditions of public trust and accountability in an era of AI-assisted enquiry.

AI-assisted enquiry opens up new interfaces with information systems, previously known only to a few. Now anyone with an LLM handy might begin reassembling the records. 

For Civic interplay the question this provokes is: What can we learn about the institutions that govern collective action and resourcing? And what can be learned when we try to find out?  

Everything here is experimental, but hopefully in pursuit of stronger places and communities, whose collective but scarce resources are ultimately governed well.
